label: Decision Spine × Counterpoint Hybrid V1

baseline.rule: Hybrid V1 must outperform Decision Spine rather than merely contain more ideas.

decisionSpine.rule: The spine appears only when there is an actual semantic relationship, provenance chain, chronology, or consequence.

counterpoint.rule: Counterpoint must improve reading and evaluation, not merely substitute a serif font.

threshold.rule: Threshold is a consequence state language, not navigation or the default product world.

proofQuestions: Are recommendations materially easier to read?
Does provenance feel meaningful without becoming a graph?
Is approval unmistakably different from advisory work?
Does Decision Detail feel durable enough to reference months later?
Does Project Memory feel editable while remaining trustworthy?
Does mobile stay calm and avoid desktop complexity?
Does the result feel uniquely AI Council rather than a styled generic AI workspace?

hardFailConditions.rule: Reject if spine decoration appears without semantic lineage.
Reject if Threshold visual language leaks into ordinary conversation or navigation.
Reject if editorial styling makes operational controls ambiguous.
Reject if visual drama reduces information density or readability.
Reject if the right context panel competes with the conversation.
Reject if approval does not visibly alter authority state.
Reject if Project Home becomes a dashboard instead of a continuation surface.
Reject if mobile restores desktop complexity.
Reject if Hybrid V1 removes canonical information to look cleaner.

comparison.question: Did Hybrid V1 materially improve the current winner?
comparison.winnerRule: Hybrid V1 may be recommended only if no hard-fail condition is triggered and its weighted review score is greater than 8.98.
